requirements.requirement: Configure node1 kernel command line so it boots with audit=1
requirements.summary: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub was updated with audit=1 (cmd-ba62cc6d51c343a2), and grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args=audit=1 applied it directly to grub.cfg for both the default and rescue kernel entries (cmd-456bf55020e84bc0), confirmed present in the on-disk linux16 lines (cmd-8f335eca559c4ae0).

requirements.requirement: audit=1 setting persists across a reboot (not just applied to the running kernel)
requirements.summary: Direct before/after transition evidence: pre-reboot baseline showed /proc/cmdline without audit=1 and auditctl enabled=0 (cmd-3cbab9c196a04cfd, boot_id 33b0e84c...). A real reboot was issued (cmd-f76cb9411bbb410f) and the node was polled until reachable again with a different boot_id (dddcd817..., cmd-fdedb0d3eb6a4365), matching the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity -> global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). Post-reboot verification shows /proc/cmdline includes audit=1, auditctl -s reports enabled=1 (changed from 0), and dmesg shows the audit subsystem initializing at boot (cmd-5453739b9ab343b9), confirming the setting survived the restart.

overall_summary: The task required node1 to boot with audit=1 persistently across reboots. The executor directly demonstrated this with a full pre/post transition: baseline state without audit=1 and auditd enabled=0, a real reboot (confirmed via changed boot_id, cross-checked against the fixed global lifecycle snapshots), and post-reboot verification that /proc/cmdline, auditctl -s, and dmesg all confirm audit=1 is active. All state-changing commands were necessary and minimal, with no residue or unnecessary mutations. Both material outcomes are satisfied with strong, coherent evidence.
limitations: No independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol output was provided beyond the single reboot performed to satisfy the task itself; since node1 is the only managed node and the task itself required a reboot, this coincides with and satisfies that expectation, but no separate/duplicate restart cycle was observed.

Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so package-manager consistency around the grubby/grub changes could not be independently verified.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 11 executor commands chronologically. The only state-changing actions were: sed edit of /etc/default/grub (cmd-ba62cc6d51c343a2) and grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args=audit=1 (cmd-456bf55020e84bc0), both directly required to satisfy the task, plus the reboot itself (cmd-f76cb9411bbb410f) which was necessary to produce bounded final evidence of persistence. Editing both /etc/default/grub and using grubby to apply the change directly to grub.cfg is a reasonable, non-redundant pairing on RHEL7 BIOS/grub2 (grubby applies immediately, /etc/default/grub keeps future grub2-mkconfig regenerations consistent) rather than an unnecessary mutation. All other commands were read-only discovery or verification. No leftover residue: /tmp entries differ only due to new systemd-private directories created automatically by the reboot itself, not executor-created files, and failed-services/listening-sockets are consistent pre/post. No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations were found.
